articles.headline: Trump says he 'loves the inflation' as US prices rise at fastest rate in three years
articles.summary: Consumers are increasingly feeling the strain of the US-Israel war in Iran.
articles._summary: President Donald Trump has said he "loves the inflation" as US prices rose last month at their fastest rate in three years. Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) figures showed prices went up by 4.2% in May from a year earlier. The increase, from 3.8% in April , was driven by rising energy costs in the wake of the US-Israel war in Iran. "I love it. The numbers were great. You know what I really love? I love the inflation," Trump said at the White House. But he promised the rising prices would "come down like a rock" when the war with Iran was over. Later in the day, the US military bombed Iran. Reacting to the inflation figures on Wednesday, the president said US forces had conducted nighttime operations to take "millions of barrels" of oil from Iran, which he said had contributed to a slight drop in oil prices. "When this conflict is over… you will see oil drop to where it was before," he told reporters in the White House.
articles._zh_headline: 特朗普表示他“喜欢通货膨胀”，因为美国物价以三年来最快的速度上涨
articles._zh_summary: 唐纳德·特朗普总统表示，他“喜欢通货膨胀”，因为上个月美国物价以三年来最快的速度上涨。美国劳工统计局 (BLS) 的数据显示，5 月份物价同比上涨 4.2%。 4月份的增长为3.8%，这是由于美以伊朗战争后能源成本上涨所致。 “我喜欢它。这些数字很棒。你知道我真正喜欢什么吗？我喜欢通货膨胀，”特朗普在白宫表示。但他承诺，当与伊朗的战争结束时，不断上涨的价格将“像岩石一样下降”。当天晚些时候，美军轰炸了伊朗。针对周三的通胀数据，总统表示，美军进行了夜间行动，从伊朗夺取了“数百万桶”石油，他称这导致油价小幅下跌。他在白宫对记者说：“当这场冲突结束后……你会看到石油价格跌至之前的水平。”

articles.headline: Veterans and relatives see no place for Trump's arch near Arlington National Cemetery
articles.summary: Three Vietnam War veterans are suing to stop President Trump from building an arch just steps from Arlington National Cemetery, where 400,000 service members, veterans and their relatives are buried.
articles._summary: Shaun Byrnes, 83, a U.S. Navy veteran who served in Vietnam, arrives for an interview near Arlington National Cemetery in Arlington, Virginia on Monday, June 8, 2026. Public Citizen, representing Byrnes and other veterans, is suing the Trump administration to block construction of the proposed Triumphal Arch in Memorial Circle. Eric Lee for NPR hide caption Some of the most forceful objections against President Trump's proposed triumphal arch are coming from — and on behalf of — veterans. That's because the 250-foot structure would be built on a roundabout near the main entrance to Arlington National Cemetery, the final resting place for over 400,000 active-duty service members, veterans and their families. The Trump administration says in its proposal that the purpose of the arch is to "celebrate the triumphs of the American people, inspire patriotism and love of country, and beautify our nation's capital."
articles._zh_headline: 退伍军人和亲属认为阿灵顿国家公墓附近没有特朗普拱门的位置
articles._zh_summary: 2026 年 6 月 8 日星期一，曾在越南服役的 83 岁美国海军退伍军人肖恩·伯恩斯 (Shaun Byrnes) 抵达弗吉尼亚州阿灵顿阿灵顿国家公墓附近接受采访。代表伯恩斯和其他退伍军人的公众公民正在起诉特朗普政府，要求阻止在纪念圈修建凯旋门。美国国家公共广播电台 (NPR) 的埃里克·李 (Eric Lee) 隐藏标题 对特朗普总统拟议的凯旋门提出的一些最强烈的反对意见来自退伍军人并代表退伍军人。这是因为这座 250 英尺高的建筑将建在阿灵顿国家公墓主入口附近的环形交叉路口上，阿灵顿国家公墓是超过 400,000 名现役军人、退伍军人及其家人的最后安息之地。特朗普政府在提案中表示，拱门的目的是“庆祝美国人民的胜利，激发爱国主义和对国家的热爱，并美化我们国家的首都”。
